answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Consistency Rule: each identity must reproduce a stable behavioural fingerprint (task mix, timing, counterparties) across epochs. Enforce by flagging identities whose fingerprint shifts beyond a tolerance, then requiring them to re-earn standing through a slow saffron-penalty period. Cost: a sybil cluster must sustain consistent behaviour across epochs, and any ripple in fingerprints forces costly re-establishment. Karst-like gaps in activity also count against consistency, so dormancy followed by sudden coordination is penalized.
